The CHECK half of the declaration is still by scenario, because the locator artefact does carry one.
the_population_this_file_declares.what_the_trailing_slash_buys_and_what_it: Each prefix ends in `/`, and the reason is PROSPECTIVE rather than live — stated that way because the first draft of this field claimed otherwise and the control measured it out. The claim was that without the slash `MCP.Transport.StreamableHTTP` would name both MCP.Transport.StreamableHTTPStatelessTest and MCP.Transport.StreamableHTTP.ACTest. That string is not one of the prefixes this selector uses: the leaves carry FULL module names, and over all 21 server modules — over all 30 in B2b — NOT ONE is a plain string-prefix of another. `mix run conformance/controls/crosswalk_controls.exs selectors` strips the slash from every leaf and measures the population unchanged, so on the shipped anchor the slash removes NOTHING. What it buys is a bound against a module ADDED LATER whose name EXTENDS one of these eight — `...DispatchTestExtra` and the like. That case has no live instance, so the control CONSTRUCTS one: a synthetic server row in an extending module, refused by the slashed selector and admitted by the slashless one, on the same fixture and in both directions. The slash is therefore kept as a discipline whose value is future, and NOT as a fact about this anchor.
the_population_this_file_declares.why_a_prefix_predicate_and_not_an_enumer: An enumeration of `key equals` leaves needs no new code and was rejected for the reason C1b-iii's `cg is_null` was chosen over one: an enumeration CANNOT DENOTE A MEMBER ADDED LATER. A new test in one of these eight modules would fall silently outside the population, and G15a — which compares the derived population against the selector's denotation — would stay green over the omission, because the omission would be in the universe as well as in the file. The prefix predicate picks the new member up and G15a then reds naming it as `missing`. The cost is one new selector leaf, and the leaf's caller is the population it was added for, so it is not S9-15's guard on a dead path.

how_a_silent_axis_was_decided: The client file's rule, applied unchanged and NOT restated here: a claim covers an axis only when an assertion's SUBJECT is the behaviour that axis names. What IS new on this leg is how often the rule bites on one axis of a two-axis check, and it bites the same way every time: eight of this file's red-OC edges are silent on an `http_status` axis and agree on a `jsonrpc_error_code` one. That is not a coincidence, it is the shape of this SDK's suite — `MCP.Server.DispatchTest` asserts below the transport and cannot see a status, and `MCP.Transport.StreamableHTTPStatelessTest` reads `error(conn)` rather than `conn.status` on every removed-method path. It is a real gap in our coverage and it is what puts those edges in 4b rather than leaving them able to reach 4a.
the_all_silent_case: THREE edges have EVERY axis silent. They are recorded and ESCALATED as `no_axis_contact`, never bucketed — A3 §2 rules that covering zero of one axis is no match rather than a partial one, generalised to N axes is exactly this, and A3 §3's table has no row for it. The client file has four of these and the rule is the same. What differs is that TWO of the three here are against a check that is RED at the accepted run (`ServerUnsupportedVersionError`), so the silence is not harmless: it is the precise reason our green tells us nothing about why the harness failed us. Each of the three says on its own record what the near-agreement was and where it stopped.
the_contradicting_edges: 5 edges carry a `contradicts` verdict and they are the first substantial disagreement the crosswalk has recorded — the client leg's three all sat on one check family. They are three findings, not five. FIRST, the `initialize` pair (inherited from C1a, moved here unchanged): this SDK answers a removed `initialize` with -32022 UnsupportedProtocolVersion where the suite requires -32601, asserted once below the transport and once over real HTTP. SECOND, the `RequestMetaInvalid` pair, authored here: a request whose `_meta` is missing is answered -32022 where the check requires -32602 Invalid params — the same disagreement about which error a stateless-core violation earns, reached by a different route, and a one-axis check so there is nothing silent to soften it. THIRD, and sharpest, `subscriptions/listen` in JSON mode: our unit asserts HTTP 200 and PASSES where the check's `http_status` axis requires 404, WHILE AGREEING with the same check's `jsonrpc_error_code` axis. Every other red-OC edge in this file is silent on `http_status` because the unit never looks; that one looked and wrote down the other answer. All five are 4a — red OC, green ET, contradicting — and none escalates, because `(red, green, :contradicting)` is a row the ratified table has.
why_contradicts_and_not_silent: `how_a_silent_axis_was_decided` is conservative about claiming COVERAGE — a claim covers an axis only when an assertion's SUBJECT is the behaviour that axis names. It is NOT a rule for suppressing disagreement, and reading it that way would make it a rule for hiding exactly what a crosswalk exists to find. The client file states this and it is cited rather than restated; what is new here is that it now decides FIVE edges instead of three, and that on this leg the two readings give visibly different answers. Each of the five carries its own `why_contradicts_and_not_silent` where the judgement is not obvious from the evidence.
what_the_red_OC_population_did_and_did_n: This is the first slice with a substantial red-OC population — 17 FAILURE and 13 SUCCESS among the declared checks, against 54 of 54 SUCCESS across the whole client leg — so it is the first at which buckets 4a and 4b are reachable on real data. Both are: 5 edges land 4a and 6 land 4b, out of 13 edges against a red check. A3 §3's THIRD combination, `(red, green, :full) -> :divergent_despite_agreement`, is STILL NOT LIVE, and that is a MEASUREMENT rather than an oversight. For it to fire, an edge would have to agree with EVERY axis of a red check. Every red check reached here either has a single axis our claims contradict (the RequestMetaInvalid family — we answer -32022 where -32602 is required) or has an `http_status` axis no unit of ours asserts: 8 of the 13 red-OC edges are silent on exactly that axis. The one unit that DOES assert a status asserts the wrong one, which is a contradiction and not an agreement. So the combination is unreachable from this slice's claims, and saying so is worth more than manufacturing an edge to reach it. The escalation is nonetheless EXERCISED on real server-stateless data by `conformance/controls/crosswalk_falsification_controls.exs escalations`, which takes a real 4b edge from this file, mutates its silent `http_status` axis to `agrees` in memory and requires the escalation to fire, then mutates the OC verdict to green on the same edge and requires it to STOP firing and bucket as 5. Both directions, because a rule that fires on everything is not discriminating and a control that only shows it firing cannot tell the difference.
